learn.hook: A chocolate bar has 12 little squares. If you eat 2 of them, what fraction have you eaten? There is more than one right name!
points: A grid is a whole cut into equal small squares.
To shade 1/8 of a grid of 8 squares, shade 1 square. For 1/8 of 16 squares, shade 2 squares.
Count all the squares (bottom number) and the shaded squares (top number).
The same shaded part can have two names: 2 out of 6 squares is 2/6, and it is also 1 of 3 equal columns, 1/3.

example.q: A grid has 12 squares. How many squares should Pooja shade to show 1/6?

learn.reallife: A ludo board, a chessboard and a tiled floor are all grids. Tiles of one colour show a fraction of the floor.

items.text: To show 1/6 of a 6-square grid, shade ___ square
To show 1/12 of a 24-square grid, shade ___ squares
2 of 6 squares shaded is 2/6, also called ___
To show 1/8 of a 16-square grid, shade ___ squares

quiz.q: A grid has 8 equal squares. How many squares show 1/8?
quiz.explain: 1/8 means 1 of 8 equal parts. With 8 squares, 1 square is one part.
quiz.mistake: Shades as many squares as the bottom number

quiz.q: A grid has 12 squares. Ravi shades 2 of them. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: 2 shaded out of 12 equal squares is 2/12.
quiz.mistake: Puts the total on top

quiz.q: To shade 1/6 of a grid with 12 squares, how many squares must be shaded?
quiz.explain: 12 squares in 6 equal parts gives 2 squares in each part. Shade one part: 2 squares.
quiz.mistake: Shades 6 squares, the bottom number

quiz.q: A grid of 6 squares is in 3 columns of 2. One column is shaded. Which two names fit?
quiz.explain: One of 3 equal columns is 1/3. It is 2 of 6 small squares, so 2/6 too.
quiz.mistake: Names only one way of counting the parts

quiz.q: Which fraction is the same shaded part as 1/3?
quiz.explain: Splitting each third into 2 gives 2 of 6 parts: 2/6 = 1/3.
quiz.mistake: Changes only the bottom number

quiz.q: A 12-square grid has 3 squares shaded. Which other fraction names it?
quiz.explain: 12 squares in 4 equal parts has 3 squares in each part. 3 shaded = 1 part of 4 = 1/4.
quiz.mistake: Uses the number shaded as the bottom number

quiz.q: Ayaan says 4 shaded squares out of 8 is 1/4. What is right?
quiz.explain: 4 out of 8 is half of the grid, so 4/8 = 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 4 shaded with 1/4

quiz.q: How many squares are there in a grid that shows 1/12 when 1 square is shaded?
quiz.explain: If 1 square is 1/12, there are 12 equal squares in all.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the bottom number to the total

teach.ask: Gappu shaded 2 of 6 squares and called it 2/6. His friend called it 1/3. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both are right! 2/6 and 1/3 are the same shaded part!
teach.nudge: Can one shaded part have two fraction names?

learn.hook: Your fraction kit has strips cut into halves, quarters, sixths and twelfths. How many ways can you build one whole strip?
points: A fraction kit has strips of the same length cut into equal pieces: 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8, 1/12 pieces.
Two 1/2 pieces make one whole. Four 1/4 pieces make one whole. Six 1/6 pieces make one whole.
Two 1/4 pieces are as long as one 1/2 piece.
We can mix pieces to make a whole: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1.
Check: the pieces must end exactly at the end of the whole strip, with no gap and no overlap.

example.q: Make a whole with one 1/2 piece and some 1/6 pieces.

learn.reallife: Cutting a pizza or a cake for friends, we fit pieces of different sizes together to make the whole.

games.title: Fraction kit facts
items: Two 1/4 pieces are as long as one 1/2 piece.
Two sixths make 1/3; three sixths make 1/2.

games.title: How many to make a whole?

quiz.q: How many 1/4 pieces make one whole strip?
quiz.explain: The whole is cut into 4 equal quarters, so 4 pieces make it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2 quarters make a whole

quiz.q: How many 1/4 pieces are as long as one 1/2 piece?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller piece can cover a bigger one alone

quiz.q: Tina has one 1/2 piece and one 1/4 piece. Which piece completes the whole?
quiz.mistake: Does not add the pieces already there

quiz.q: Which set makes exactly one whole?
quiz.mistake: Adds the bottom numbers

quiz.q: Raju has one 1/2 piece. How many 1/6 pieces does he need to finish the whole?
quiz.explain: 1/2 = 3/6. A whole is 6/6. 6/6 − 3/6 = 3/6, so three 1/6 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Uses 6 because the bottom number is 6

quiz.q: How many 1/12 pieces make one whole?
quiz.explain: 12 twelfths make a whole: 12/12 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Confuses with half of 12

quiz.q: Meera uses two 1/4 pieces and some 1/12 pieces to make a whole. How many 1/12 pieces?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change quarters to twelfths

quiz.q: Which set does NOT make one whole?
quiz.mistake: Thinks any three pieces make a whole

teach.ask: Gappu has a 1/2 strip and two 1/4 strips. Do they make a whole strip? How do I know?
teach.praise: Yes! Two quarters make a half, and two halves make a whole!
teach.nudge: What do two 1/4 pieces make together?

learn.hook: Is 5/10 of a roti the same as half a roti? Let us check with our fraction kit!
points: Many fractions are equal to 1/2: 2/4, 3/6, 4/8, 5/10, 6/12.
A fraction is equal to 1/2 when its top number is half of its bottom number.
To find how many small pieces make a bigger piece, see how many fit along it: two 1/8 pieces make 1/4.
Shortcut: 1/4 ÷ 1/8 means 'how many eighths in a quarter' — 8 ÷ 4 = 2.
Smaller pieces (bigger bottom number) are needed in larger numbers to cover the same length.

example.q: How many 1/12 pieces make one 1/3 piece?

learn.reallife: Two 50 paise coins make ₹1, and four 25 paise coins make ₹1 — small pieces make a bigger one!

quiz.q: Which of these fractions equals one half?
quiz.explain: 4 is half of 8, so 4/8 = 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Picks any fraction with a 4 or an 8

quiz.q: 5/10 of a ribbon is cut. Is that half?
options: No, it is more than half
No, it is less than half
quiz.explain: 5 is half of 10, so 5/10 = 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only 1/2 itself means half

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/4?
quiz.explain: 1/4 = 2/8, so two 1/8 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way

quiz.q: How many 1/6 pieces make 1/2?
quiz.explain: 1/2 = 3/6, so three 1/6 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Uses the bottom number 2

quiz.q: How many 1/12 pieces make 1/4?
quiz.explain: 1/4 = 3/12, so three 1/12 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Uses 4 because of the 1/4

quiz.q: 6/? = 1/2. What number goes in the box?
quiz.explain: The bottom must be double the top. 6 × 2 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Halves instead of doubling

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT equal to 1/2?
quiz.explain: Half of 7 is 3 1/2, not 3, so 3/7 is not 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any fraction with a small top number is half

quiz.q: Kiran fits 1/8 pieces along a 1/2 piece. How many does she need?
quiz.explain: 1/2 = 4/8, so 4 eighths fit.
quiz.mistake: Counts only 2 because of 1/2

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 3/6 and 1/2 are different because the numbers are different. How can I check?
teach.praise: I see! 3 is half of 6, so 3/6 is the same as 1/2!
teach.nudge: How do the top and bottom numbers of a half fraction compare?

learn.hook: Riya cuts her roti into 4 pieces and eats 2. Arjun cuts his into 8 and eats 4. Who ate more? Surprise: the same!
points: A fraction is a part of a whole cut into equal parts. 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts.
The top number is the numerator. The bottom number is the denominator.
Equivalent fractions show the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8.
Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number to get an equivalent fraction.
Equivalent fractions sit on the same spot on a number line.

example.q: Riya eats 2/4 of a roti. Arjun eats 4/8 of the same size roti. Who ate more?

learn.reallife: When you share a pizza or a chikki bar, cutting it into more pieces does not change how much you get.

games.title: True or false?
items: 5/10 is 5 of 10 parts, which is half.
2/4 is half, but 2/8 is only a quarter.
Adding the same number to the top and bottom always gives an equivalent fraction.
1/2 → 2/3 by adding 1, but 2/3 is not half.
Multiplying top and bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
All 3 of the 3 parts make the whole.

quiz.q: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
quiz.explain: 3/6 means 3 of 6 equal parts. That is half of the whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a fraction with a 1 or 2 in it must be half

quiz.q: A chikki bar has 8 equal pieces. Meena eats 2. What fraction did she eat, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 2 of 8 is 2/8. Divide top and bottom by 2: 1/4.
quiz.mistake: Counts eaten pieces against pieces left (2/6)

quiz.q: 3/4 = ?/12. What number goes in the box?
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Changes only the bottom number

quiz.q: Kabir says 2/3 = 4/9 because 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 3 = 9. Is he right?
options: No, he must multiply top and bottom by the same number
quiz.explain: He used × 2 on top but × 3 at the bottom. 2/3 = 4/6 or 6/9, not 4/9.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies top and bottom by different numbers

quiz.q: Which pair of fractions are equivalent?
quiz.explain: 2/5: multiply top and bottom by 2 → 4/10. Same amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fractions with the same denominator or the same digits must be equal

quiz.q: Harpreet folds a paper into 3 equal parts and colours 1 part. Then she folds each part in half. How many small parts are coloured now?
quiz.explain: The paper now has 6 small parts. The coloured third is now 2 small parts: 1/3 = 2/6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks folding again does not change the number of coloured pieces

quiz.q: On a number line from 0 to 1, which fraction lands on the same spot as 1/2?
quiz.explain: 5/10 means 5 of 10 equal jumps, which is exactly halfway.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1/5 or 1/10 is close to 1/2 because they start with 1

quiz.q: 4/5 = 16/?. What number goes in the box?
quiz.explain: 4 × 4 = 16, so multiply the bottom by 4: 5 × 4 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 12 to the bottom because 12 was added to the top

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: 'How can 1/2 and 2/4 be the same?'
teach.praise: Yay! Cutting into more pieces but taking more pieces keeps it the same!
teach.nudge: How do I make a new fraction that is the same? What do I do to the top and the bottom?

learn.hook: Why say 12/18 of a laddoo box when you can just say 2/3? Let's make fractions tiny and neat!
points: To simplify, divide the top and the bottom by the same number.
A fraction is in simplest form when no number except 1 divides both top and bottom.
Dividing by the biggest common number gets you there in one step.
Simplifying does not change the amount, only the way we write it.
learn.reallife: Cooks and shopkeepers say 'half a kilo' instead of '500/1000 of a kilo'. Simple is easier!

items.text: To simplify, divide top and bottom by the ___ number

quiz.q: Write 6/8 in simplest form.
quiz.explain: Divide top and bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Divides only the top number

quiz.q: What is 10/15 in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Both 10 and 15 can be divided by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 5 from the top and bottom instead of dividing

quiz.q: What is 9/12 in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Both 9 and 12 can be divided by 3: 9/12 = 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Divides the top by 3 but the bottom by a different number

quiz.q: Aisha has 20 marbles. 15 are blue. What fraction is blue, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 15 of 20 is 15/20. Divide top and bottom by 5: 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Finds the fraction that is NOT blue, or divides wrongly

quiz.q: Which fraction is already in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Only 1 divides both 5 and 7. The others can be divided by 2 or 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a fraction with small numbers is always simplest

quiz.q: Joseph divides the top of 8/12 by 4 and the bottom by 2, and gets 2/6. What went wrong?
options: He must divide top and bottom by the same number
He should change only the top
quiz.explain: 8/12 ÷ 4 on both gives 2/3. Using different numbers changes the amount.
quiz.mistake: Divides top and bottom by different numbers

quiz.q: A box had 18 laddoos. 12 were eaten at a Diwali party. What fraction was eaten, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 12/18. Divide both by 6: 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Writes the fraction of laddoos left (1/3) instead of eaten

quiz.q: To simplify 16/24 in one step, which is the biggest number that divides both 16 and 24?
quiz.explain: 8 divides 16 (2 times) and 24 (3 times). No bigger number divides both. 16/24 = 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a common number that is not the biggest

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I make 6/9 simpler?'
teach.praise: Neat! Divide top and bottom by the same number. 6/9 is 2/3!
teach.nudge: What do I do to the numbers? And do I do it to both of them?

topics.title: Checking equal fractions and using < and >

learn.hook: Is 3/4 the same as 9/12? Is 2/3 more than 5/8? Let us be fraction judges!
points: To check if two fractions are equal, rewrite them with the same bottom number (a common denominator).
If the tops are the same after that, the fractions are equal. If not, the bigger top is the bigger fraction.
Use > for 'is greater than', < for 'is less than' and = for 'is equal to'. The open mouth faces the bigger number.
learn.reallife: Comparing fractions helps choose the bigger share — 3/4 of a pizza or 2/3 of the same pizza?

quiz.q: Are 2/3 and 8/12 equal?
quiz.mistake: Does not multiply both numbers by the same number

quiz.q: Which sign goes in 3/8 ☐ 1/4?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: Which sign goes in 5/12 ☐ 1/2?
quiz.mistake: Compares only the top numbers

quiz.q: Which sign goes in 4/6 ☐ 2/3?
quiz.explain: 2/3 = 4/6, so they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different numbers mean different amounts

quiz.q: Which fraction completes 3/5 = ?/10?
quiz.mistake: Changes only the bottom number

quiz.q: Which statement is true?
quiz.mistake: Compares top numbers without a common bottom

quiz.q: Sonu says 2/5 and 3/10 are equal. To check, he writes 2/5 with bottom 10. What does he get?
quiz.explain: 2/5 = 4/10, which is more than 3/10.
quiz.mistake: Changes the bottom without changing the top

quiz.q: Which is the right way to write 'one-sixth is less than one-third'?
quiz.explain: The < sign means 'is less than', with the smaller number on the left.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the < and > signs

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if 2/4 and 3/6 are equal. How can I check them?
teach.praise: Both become 6/12, so they are equal! Thanks!
teach.nudge: What can I do to the bottom numbers before comparing?

learn.hook: Would you rather have 1/3 of a big cake or 1/5 of it? Think before you answer!
points: Same bottom number: the bigger top number is bigger. 5/7 > 3/7.
Same top number: the smaller bottom number is bigger, because the pieces are bigger. 1/3 > 1/5.
Different bottoms: make equivalent fractions with the same bottom, then compare.
Using 1/2 as a helper: 5/8 is more than half, 3/8 is less than half.

example.q: Riya eats 2/3 of a cake. Arjun eats 3/4 of the same size cake. Who eats more?

learn.reallife: When friends share sweets, rotis or a cricket field for practice, comparing fractions keeps it fair.

games.title: Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Arrange the fractions from smallest to largest

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 3/7 or 5/7?
quiz.explain: The pieces are the same size (sevenths). 5 pieces are more than 3 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fractions are equal because the bottoms match

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/5?
quiz.explain: Cutting into 3 gives bigger pieces than cutting into 5. So 1/3 > 1/5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: Riya ate 2/3 of a dosa. Kabir ate 3/4 of the same size dosa. Who ate more?
quiz.explain: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. 9/12 is more, so Kabir ate more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2/3 and 3/4 are equal because each is one piece short of a whole

quiz.q: Which fraction is more than 1/2?
quiz.explain: Half of 8 is 4. 5/8 has 5 parts, more than 4, so it is more than half.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction with a big denominator

quiz.q: Put 3/8, 1/2 and 1/4 in order from smallest. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: In eighths: 1/4 = 2/8, 3/8, 1/2 = 4/8. So 3/8 is in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Orders by the bottom numbers only

quiz.q: Meena drank 5/6 of a glass of lassi. Aisha drank 7/12 of the same glass. Who drank more?
quiz.explain: 5/6 = 10/12. 10/12 is more than 7/12, so Meena drank more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fraction with bigger numbers (7/12) is bigger

quiz.q: Which is the largest: 2/3, 3/5 or 1/2?
quiz.mistake: Picks the fraction with the biggest top number

quiz.q: In a race, Arjun has run 3/10 of the track and Harpreet has run 2/5. Who is ahead?
quiz.explain: 2/5 = 4/10. 4/10 is more than 3/10, so Harpreet is ahead.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3/10 is more because 3 > 2

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: 'Is 1/4 bigger than 1/3, because 4 is bigger than 3?'
teach.praise: Oh! More pieces means smaller pieces. 1/3 is bigger. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What happens to the size of each piece when we cut into more parts? How do we compare when bottoms are different?

learn.hook: Dadi made parathas and cut each into halves. Seven halves were eaten. How many whole parathas is that?
points: When we count pieces from more than one whole, the fraction can be more than 1.
7 halves = 7/2. Two halves make a whole, so 7 halves = 3 wholes and 1 half.
A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part: 7/2 = 3 1/2.
To change, divide the top by the bottom: 11/4 → 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so 11/4 = 2 3/4.
Counting quarters: 4 quarters = 1 whole, 8 quarters = 2 wholes.
learn.reallife: At a party, 13 quarter slices of cake are served — that is 3 whole cakes and one more quarter!

quiz.q: Seven half-parathas were eaten. How many parathas is that?
quiz.explain: 2 halves make 1 paratha. 7 halves = 3 wholes and 1 half = 3 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Counts the pieces as wholes

quiz.q: Mum cut apples into quarters. 12 quarters were used for chaat. How many whole apples?
quiz.explain: 4 quarters make 1 apple. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 apples.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 instead of 4

quiz.q: Write 11/4 as a mixed number.
quiz.explain: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so 2 wholes and 3 quarters.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the whole and the remainder

quiz.q: Write 5/3 as a mixed number.
quiz.explain: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 remainder 2, so 1 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Uses the quotient as the top number

quiz.q: Which fraction is the same as 2 1/2?
quiz.explain: 2 wholes = 4 halves, plus 1 half = 5 halves = 5/2.
quiz.mistake: Writes the whole number as the top number

quiz.q: Rahul ate 3 halves of a roti and Ria ate 2 halves. How many rotis did they eat together?
quiz.explain: 3 halves + 2 halves = 5 halves = 2 1/2 rotis.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 2 halves make one roti

quiz.q: How many quarters are there in 3 whole cakes?
quiz.explain: Each cake has 4 quarters. 3 × 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 4

quiz.q: Which is a fraction greater than 1?
quiz.explain: In 9/4 the top is bigger than the bottom, so it is more than one whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number makes it bigger

teach.ask: Gappu has 9 half-laddoos. He thinks that is 9 laddoos. Can you help me count properly?
teach.praise: Two halves make one laddoo, so 9 halves are 4 1/2 laddoos!
teach.nudge: How many halves make one whole laddoo?

topics.title: Fractions more than 1 on the number line

learn.hook: An ant walks 1/4 cm with each step. After 16 steps, how far has it gone?
points: Fractions greater than 1 sit to the right of 1 on a number line: 3/2 is between 1 and 2.
If the top number is less than the bottom, the fraction is less than 1 (3/5).
If the top equals the bottom, the fraction equals 1 (5/5). If the top is bigger, it is more than 1 (7/5).
Adding the same fraction again and again is like jumping on a number line: 16 jumps of 1/4 = 16/4 = 4.
Each 4 jumps of 1/4 reach the next whole number.

example.q: A frog makes 10 jumps of 1/2 m. Where does it land?

learn.reallife: A ruler is a number line: 1 1/2 cm is halfway between 1 and 2.

games.title: Less than, equal to or more than 1?
Left to right on the number line

quiz.q: Sixteen ants stand in a line. Each ant is 1/4 cm long. How long is the line?
quiz.explain: 16 × 1/4 = 16/4 = 4 cm. Every 4 ants make 1 cm.
quiz.mistake: Counts the ants as cm

quiz.q: Between which two whole numbers does 7/4 lie?
quiz.explain: 7/4 = 1 3/4, so it lies between 1 and 2.
quiz.mistake: Reads the top number as the position

quiz.q: Which fraction is equal to 1?
quiz.explain: When top and bottom are equal, the fraction is one whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1/8 means one

quiz.q: Which fraction is less than 1?
quiz.explain: 6 is less than 7, so 6/7 is less than a whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom makes it more than 1

quiz.q: A grasshopper makes 6 jumps of 1/2 m. How far does it go?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 2 instead of halving

quiz.q: How many jumps of 1/3 reach 2 on the number line?
quiz.explain: 3 jumps of 1/3 reach 1, so 6 jumps reach 2.
quiz.mistake: Counts only to 1

quiz.q: Which is the right order from left to right on a number line?
quiz.explain: Same bottom: bigger top is further right. 2 < 4 < 5.
quiz.mistake: Puts bigger numbers on the left

quiz.q: Riya walks 5 laps of 1/4 km. How far does she walk?
quiz.mistake: Counts laps as km

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if 9/7 is more or less than 1. How can I tell quickly?
teach.praise: The top 9 is bigger than the bottom 7, so 9/7 is more than 1!
teach.nudge: Which two numbers should I compare in the fraction?

learn.hook: Is 5/9 of a mango more than half? Is 4/3 more than a whole? Two helper numbers, 1 and 1/2, can tell you fast!
points: If one fraction is more than 1 and the other is less than 1, the one more than 1 is bigger: 5/4 > 7/8.
A fraction equals 1/2 when its top is exactly half its bottom: 4/8, 7/14.
A fraction is less than 1/2 when its top is less than half its bottom: in 3/8, half of 8 is 4, and 3 < 4.
A fraction is more than 1/2 when its top is more than half its bottom: 5/8.
Compare two fractions by checking which side of 1/2 each lies on: 3/7 < 1/2 < 4/6.
learn.reallife: When you see 'more than half the seats are full' at a cinema, you are using the benchmark 1/2!

games.title: Benchmark check
items: 6/5 is bigger than 9/10 because 6/5 is more than 1.
6 is exactly half of 12, so it equals 1/2.

quiz.q: Which is greater: 5/4 or 7/8?
quiz.explain: 5/4 is more than 1, and 7/8 is less than 1. So 5/4 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fraction with bigger numbers is bigger

quiz.q: Which fraction is exactly half?
quiz.explain: 7 is exactly half of 14.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction close to half

quiz.q: Why is 3/8 less than 1/2?
options: Half of 8 is 4, and 3 is less than 4
quiz.explain: For 1/2 the top would be 4. Since 3 < 4, 3/8 is less than half.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that has nothing to do with half

quiz.q: Which fraction is less than 1/2?
quiz.explain: Half of 9 is 4 1/2. 4 < 4 1/2, so 4/9 is less than half.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any fraction with top 4 is small

quiz.q: Using 1/2, compare 2/5 and 4/7.
quiz.explain: 2/5 is less than half (half of 5 is 2 1/2). 4/7 is more than half (half of 7 is 3 1/2). So 2/5 < 4/7.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the top numbers

quiz.q: Which fraction is more than 1?
quiz.explain: In 10/9 the top is bigger than the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which number is the top

quiz.q: Aman ate 3/7 of a cake and Lata ate 5/8 of the same size cake. Who ate more?
quiz.explain: 3/7 is less than half and 5/8 is more than half, so Lata ate more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger bottom number means less cake for Lata

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: 2/9 is less than half, 1/2 is half, 7/6 is more than 1.
quiz.mistake: Orders by the size of the bottom numbers

teach.ask: Gappu must decide if 4/9 or 5/8 of a watermelon is bigger without a common bottom. How can 1/2 help me?
teach.praise: 4/9 is less than half and 5/8 is more than half, so 5/8 is bigger. Smart!
teach.nudge: Which side of 1/2 is each fraction on?
